These enemies, with enough defenses, can be beaten easily even with stuns in play. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing; towers shouldn’t be necessary/grant a massive boost in any specific thing (looking at you, Farm…). Her utility stretches over to Polluted Wasteland II, where she is essential to beating the Nuclear Monster and some other enemies like the Warden. matches.title: TDS’ Late Game Problem
matches.snippet: TDS’ Late Game Problem Introduction - Portal To Hell TDS has a late game problem; here’s why, in a massive wall of text. Already lost interest? Fine, this isn’t for you, then. If not, buckle up. DPS towers have always triumphed as the most important tower type in the game; this sentiment has grown further as more are introduced, powercreep accelerates and enemies get beefier. This is an issue, however; everything in TDS’ late game is dealt with the exact same way with very few exceptions. A lock-and-key design. Don’t believe me? Keep reading. Feigned Variety - Desolate Dystopia As I’ve said, DPS towers define the late game. They are not only all you need, but mandatory in most cases. Bring the towers with the strongest DPS in order to overcome the late game; simple as that. The options are laid out clear for you: Gatling Gun, Ranger, Engineer, and support towers. Why bring anything else? There’s no incentive except to intentionally handicap yourself and go off-meta. Harder and harder modes, however, make this less of an option. Sure, you have a massive inventory of towers, and some of them can work, but realistically, you wouldn’t bring them in if you were trying to win. And even if you do, well, what change is there? It was most notable for adding the Lunar Overture Event. But aside from that, it came with another long list of balance changes, and finally new towers after 10 months. Let’s dive in. NEW TOWERS Necromancer - This tower was actually added 3 days later on v1.9.0g. It was unlocked from the shop with 1,800 Gems. The Necromancer was quite a complicated tower. At early levels, it fires magic bolts, which at Level 1+ , can pierce through enemies. At Level 4, this is replaced by a beam fired from its book, which are not projectiles and can hit up to 4 enemies at once. That’s not what the tower really is about though. It has a “Soul Meter” stat which it fills up by simply damaging enemies, when it becomes full, it creates a gravestone near it on the path, having a maximum of 6. It can destroy its gravestones using its “Raise the Dead” ability, which periodically stops it from attacking, these gravestones will then summon random units, and any units spawned by the previous use of the ability will be killed. At Level 4, these gravestones also explode when destroyed, dealing damage. The tower had very expensive prices, costing $45,000 to max out, and it had a placement limit of 3. At Level 0-1, it just spawns Skeletons, which just collide with enemies, having a low amount of health. At Level 1, it can now spawn Sword Skeletons, which deal melee damage. At Level 2, Skeletons are upgraded to Giant Skeletons, having way more health, and Sword Skeletons are upgraded to Skeleton Knights. At Level 3, Giant Skeletons are upgraded to Hallow Guards, and Necromancer can now summon an Executioner Skeleton, having long range, and throwing an axe to deal quick ticks of damage, which then returns after 4 seconds, and it also had a lot of health. As for the overall stats of the Necromancer, its single-target DPS was abysmal for its cost, but that doesn’t really matter, because it is able to hit multiple enemies, so even the Necromancer itself deals with hordes well. The skeletons themselves are much more powerful though when stacked, especially the Executioner Skeleton. The tower is best used for late-game since the early units are very weak. But honestly, the tower is just… unreliable. The skeletons spawned by the ability are completely random every time, and the ability also kills the previously spawned skeletons and periodically stops the Necromancer from attacking, and even then the skeletons die easily when not used right. Don’t get me wrong, the tower is fun to use, especially and can be strong when used right at max level, but it’s just not really reliable. It lands a spot on high C tier. Jester - Added on November 12th, 2023, along with Act 3, the final act of the event, with the Jester being the tower reward for beating it. It threw a bomb at enemies, which obviously dealt splash damage, and it gets two bombs at Level 4. The tower was mainly focused on debuffs, with different types of bombs providing different effects.. The first type of bomb, being the fire bomb which is unlocked at Level 0, obviously deals burn damage, and surprisingly the tower’s DPS is really good for its cost with these fire bombs, and it still deals hordes really well with its splash damage and high burn damage. At Level 2, it can now use ice bombs, which freezes affected enemies for 2 seconds, but decreases Jester’s DPS a lot. At Level 3, it can now use poison bombs, which leaves an acid puddle upon exploding that lasts for 10 seconds, and dealing damage-over-time to enemies, though its single-target DPS was really low and the bombs don’t even splash damage. At Level 4, it can now use confusion bombs, which causes enemies to walk backwards for 3 seconds, being an 8 second cooldown after for each Jester. However, the confusion bombs affected MAJOR BOSSES, such as Fallen King, Nuclear Monster, and Void Reaver, overall making the tower extremely potent with stalling and debuffing enemies. Use fire bombs for DPS, and the ice and confusion bombs for stalling (but NEVER use ice with fire now due to a new rework for the debuff system). The confusion bombs being able to affect major bosses just trivialized the game. (feels like pre-bugfix Toxic Gunner all over again). In fact, it made soloing Hardcore possible again after several months. Even outside of its stalling and debuffing use, the tower was good for early-game with its high splash damage and very cheap cost, only costing $9,350 to max out, and if that wasn’t enough, it also had instant hidden detection at Level 0, and it can be even used as early-game defense in Hardcore since it had lead penetration with its splash damage. It can hit many enemies as long as it still has health, and it can deal more damage than its health, as the damage it deals to an enemy is the same as its full health, but an enemy’s defense can decrease it. The second type is the landmine unlocked at Level 3, which explodes upon an enemy steps on it, dealing splash damage to all enemies caught in the radius, as well as burning them, also decreasing an enemy’s defense by 7.5% per every tick with a maximum of 50% at Level 4. The third one is the bear trap unlocked at Level 4. Unlike the previous two traps, it can only hit a single enemy, but deals more damage. Upon contact, it stuns the enemy hit for 3 seconds. With this info provided, it seems like the Trapper is an amazing tower fulfilling different roles. The spike traps are good for early-game, the landmines are good for crowds, and the bear traps are good for stalling. Unfortunately, it takes a very long time to build up all of its traps, so you’d have to place it at the back of the map, so prepare for your matches to take very long in early-game, even then there are much better options for early-game, and its cost-for-DPS efficiency at later levels is absolutely atrocious. The main problem with Trapper is that it just doesn’t work in TDS’ core design, past early-game, Trapper is really only good for catching leaks, and if enemies leak past your main DPS spot, you just panic and lose the game. If you leak enemies a lot, you should just bring a much better tower to not leak enemies in the first place. Trapper was just not very practical to use during its early stages of release, so Trapper lands a spot on E tier, one of the worst towers in the game, even worse than Scout. It wasn't as focused on tower balancing as the previous three updates, more so on QoL and UI changes. It did rework two towers though. BALANCE CHANGES Demoman Now has to aim before attacking enemies at Level 0-2. It will focus on one enemy while aiming and will not switch to a different one if it dies or leaves its range. Projectiles now land behind the aimed enemy. Level 0 Cost: $300 -> $400 Damage: 3 -> 4 Firerate: 2.508s -> 3.008s Range: 7 -> 8 Explosion Range: 2.5 -> 2.75 Added Aim Time of 1s Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $150 -> $100 Damage: 3 -> 4 Firerate: 2.008s -> 2.658s Range remains at 10 Explosion Range: 2.5 -> 2.75 Level 2 Damage: 6 -> 8 Firerate: 2.008s -> 2.658s Range remains at 10 Explosion Range remains at 3.25 Level 3 Damage remains at 12 Firerate remains at 1.508s Range: 10 -> 12 Explosion Range remains at 3.25 Removes 1s Aim Time Increases projectile speed Level 4 Damage remains at 28 Firerate remains at 1.208s Range remains at 14 Explosion Range remains at 4 Honestly, Demoman just got worse, more specifically Level 0-2. The aim time doesn't actually affect its firerate, but the actual firerate stat became slower, so even with increased damage, its DPS remains practically the exact same, and also its range, except for Level 0 and 3. Speaking of Level 0, it got a lot worse because you used to be able to place 2 Demomen at the start, now you can only place 1. And… Level 3-4 are literally the exact same as before, except for Level 3 only getting two more range. Demoman is still a decent early-game tower for beginners, just worse than before, so it drops a few placements in C tier. Accelerator Damage values no longer fluctuate. Burst Time stat replaced with Overcharge stat. Level 0 Cost: $3,500 -> $4,250 Damage: 6-8 -> 10 Range: 13 -> 17.5 Overcharge of 180 added Level 1 Upgrade Cost: $600 -> $800 Damage: 6-8 -> 14 Range: 16 -> 17.5 Level 2 Upgrade Cost: $1,200 -> $1,350 Damage: 6-8 -> 14 Range: 16 -> 17.5 Increases Overcharge to 280 Level 3 Upgrade Cost: $3,200 -> $3,300 Damage: 11-15 -> 25 Range: 16 -> 17.5 Increases Overcharge to 425 Level 4 Upgrade Cost: $9,500 -> $10,0000 Damage: 11-15 -> 36 Tick: 0.108s -> 0.208s Range: 19 -> 17.5 Increases Overcharge to 1,080 Level 5 Direct Damage: 25-35 -> 50 Tick remains at 0.108s Range: 20 -> 22.5 Increases Overcharge to 3,000 Accelerator got a pretty massive rework. Its hidden (and annoying) mechanic of its fluctuating damage was finally removed, letting its DPS stay consistent. Its Burst Time was replaced with Overcharge, which is now a meter it has to fill up before cooling down and charging-up again. With the massively increased damage, its new DPS at all levels is actually higher than its old maximum DPS, and you also have its slightly extra range, with these coming at the cost of increased upgrade prices (going from $48,000 total at max to $49,700, barely anything at late-game), which is very well worth it. Its DPS at max is now 286.26 (higher than its old average of 208.33 and maximum of 243.06). With Commander's 55% firerate buff (only affecting tickrate, not charge-up and cooldown), that goes up to 360.57, with 8 Accelerators, that's now an outstanding 2,884.56! There's very little doubt that Accelerator is back to being the best late-game DPS tower. Its charge-up and cooldown mechanics still make it vulnerable to stuns, but that's something a Medic can solve. Accelerator goes up from #6 to #3 on the ranking.
